chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man from his companions, said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'My servants have not drawn closer to Me with anything more beloved to Me than three characteristics.' Musa said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He said: 'O Musa, asceticism in the world, and piety from disobediences, and weeping from My fear.'

Musa said: 'O Lord, so what is for the one who does that?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'O Musa! As for those ascetic in the world, they are in Paradise; and as for those weeping from My fear, they are in the Lofty Highest, no one shares with them; and as for those pious from My disobediences, I examine the people and do not examine them.'

key_terms.أُفَتِّشُ: I examine/scrutinize (referring to the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.الرَّفِيعُ الْأَعْلَى: The Lofty Highest, a high rank in Paradise
key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety or caution regarding sins and doubtful matters

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics most beloved to God for drawing closer to Him, and what are their respective rewards?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys a divine message to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) identifying asceticism (*zuhd*), piety (*wara'*), and weeping from fear (*bukaa'*) as the most beloved acts of worship to God. The text distinguishes the rewards for each: ascetics enter Paradise, those who weep from fear attain the exclusive highest ranks (*al-rafi' al-a'la*), and the pious are spared from detailed scrutiny on the Day of Judgment. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on inner emotional states, particularly weeping, as a direct path to spiritual elevation and divine intimacy.
